messages:
jamie: FYI -- EU-W2 scheduled rack drain tomorrow 03:30 UTC. We'll lose ~48 GPU slots for ~2h. Need quick plan for tenant slot reservation and user-facing degradation surface. Noticed cross-AZ fills last time that spiked bills. Anyone owning routing/cost tradeoffs?
vikram: I saw the billing delta too. If we naively backfill from other AZs, egress + cross-az GPU time kills margins. Can we prefer local-hot standby first, then soft-fill remote only if latency delta < 8ms?
sre-jen: +1 on soft-fill. Also telemetry shows a lot of short-lived KV-cache warmups after drains. Proposal: implement "warm-slot" soft-lease (default 5m) that keeps a tiny GRPC affinity to preserve KV cache without charging full reserved pricing. If warm-slot unused, it frees earlier.
jamie: That sounds promising. How would we expose it to customers? flag, default? billing change?
sre-jen: Default opt-in for Dedicated customers during maintenance windows. Billing: charge 10% of slot rate while in warm state, full rate if actively executing. We can implement via router labels + charge-window.
ops-bot: Deploy check: warm-slot feature depends on router v2.1 and billing-service feature-flag `warm_leases`. Current canary in staging passed.
maria: Two operational notes: 1) need to avoid warm-slots piling up when many tenants are in soft-lease; add global cap per AZ. 2) ensure scheduling priority still favors pinned Dedicated slices.
vikram: Agreed. Proposed config (pseudo):
```
routing:
  warm_slot:
    enabled: true
    default_ttl_seconds: 300
    billing_rate_multiplier: 0.10
    cross_az_fill:
      max_latency_ms: 8
      allowed_when_capacity_pct_below: 60
    az_global_cap: 100
```
jamie: Nice. Who can own rollout? I can take rollout plan and comms for customer impact. Need SRE runbook update and cost projection.
sre-jen: I'll update runbook and add canary to eu-staging tonight. I'll instrument metrics: warm_slot_count, warm_slot_to_active_transition_rate, avg_kvcache_hit_delta.
nana-cost: I'll run a quick model on projected revenue impact and worst-case cross-az spend if we enable warm-fill. Expect <0.8% revenue delta if caps hold, but un-capped scenarios could be ~3-4% for short windows.
maria: Can we set a temporary hard cap = 50 for the maintenance window and monitor?
vikram: yes do that. Also add a fallback policy: if avg latency from cross-az fill > 12ms for 1m, immediately stop cross-az warm-fill and only allow local.
jamie: Plan: (1) SRE deploy canary warm-slot to eu-staging tonight, (2) cost run by ana, (3) cap = 50 during maintenance, (4) routing policy enforce latency cutoff. If all green, enable during maintenance tomorrow and monitor metrics dashboard.
sre-jen: I'll post the runbook snippet once canary is live and add a short pager rule if warm_slot_to_active_transition_rate spikes > 20% above baseline.
jamie: Thanks everyone. tagging @maria @vikram for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
